question_text: A 57-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 2-year history of fatigue, worsening shortness of breath, and a productive cough for 2 years. He has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past 40 years. Examination shows pursed-lip breathing and an increased anteroposterior chest diameter. There is diffuse wheezing bilaterally and breath sounds are distant. Which of the following parameters is most likely to be decreased in this patient?

Key findings include pursed-lip breathing, increased anteroposterior chest diameter (suggesting hyperinflation), and distant breath sounds (indicating airflow limitation). In emphysema, lung elastic recoil is compromised due to the destruction of alveolar walls, leading to decreased lung elastic recoil. This aligns with the consensus that in COPD, particularly emphysema, lung elastic recoil is decreased due to loss of elastic fibers. Therefore, the most likely parameter to be decreased in this patient is lung elastic recoil.
